claims.text: Finer grain structures in AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 promote rapid and uniform outward diffusion of oxide-forming elements, especially Cr and Ti.
The enhanced outward diffusion in finer-grained material is caused by increased grain-boundary density.
Enhanced Cr and Ti diffusion leads to formation and retention of a continuous, adherent CrTaO4-based oxide layer.
A continuous, adherent CrTaO4-based oxide layer imparts high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Spark plasma sintering and subsequent annealing can be adjusted to produce distinct fine- and coarse-grained AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 samples.
Fine- and coarse-grained samples will be compared under otherwise identical oxidation treatments.
The proposed oxidation exposure is isothermal oxidation in air at 1000–1100 °C for up to 200 hours.
Grain boundaries provide enhanced diffusion pathways for oxide-forming elements.
Higher grain-boundary density accelerates transport of Cr and Ti to the alloy surface.
Coarse-grained material has fewer grain boundaries and therefore forms oxide more slowly and discontinuously.
Slower and more discontinuous oxide formation in the coarse-grained alloy produces higher oxidation rates.
Fine-grained samples will develop a denser and more coherent oxide layer than the coarse-grained baseline.
Fine-grained samples will exhibit lower oxidation kinetics, including reduced weight gain, relative to the coarse-grained baseline.
The proposed mechanism is expected to dominate at 1000–1100 °C under the specified processing and oxidation conditions.
Phase transformations induced by grain refinement may limit or confound the proposed mechanism.
Weight gain, oxide-scale morphology and continuity, and phase constitution can distinguish the fine- and coarse-grained responses.
Failure of the fine-grained samples to show a more coherent, protective scale or lower oxidation kinetics than the coarse-grained samples would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated alloy AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 contains no Ta, yet the proposed protective phase is CrTaO4 and no external Ta source or Ta-bearing addition is specified.
The mechanism emphasizes Ti transport as a driver of the named CrTaO4 scale, but Ti is not a constituent of CrTaO4; the role or resulting oxide phase of Ti is not explained.
